title: SVO word-order transfer
context_note: The verb must come at the end of the sentence.

title: Nominative particle omission (ga)
context_note: 好き takes が for the thing that is liked.

title: Topic marker confusion (ga for wa)
context_note: Plain self-introduction. 私が学生です is only right when answering 'who is the student?'.

title: Locative substitution (ni for de)
learner_input_ja: 私は図書館に勉強します。
accepted_answers_ja: 私は図書館で勉強します。
context_note: The place where an action happens takes で.

title: Word-for-word spatial translation (no ue)
learner_input_ja: 私はいすの上に座ります。
context_note: Malay 'di atas' carried over literally as の上.

title: Accusative particle drop (o)
context_note: Dropping を happens in casual speech; this case expects the polite written form.

title: Verb conjugation (past used for habitual present)
intended_meaning_ms: Saya pergi ke sekolah setiap hari.
intended_meaning_en: I go to school every day.
learner_input_ja: 毎日学校に行きました。
context_note: Malay verbs do not mark tense; a habit uses the present form.

title: Politeness mismatch
intended_meaning_en: (To a lecturer) Teacher, are you coming tomorrow?
context_note: Talking to a lecturer needs the polite form. The honorific いらっしゃいますか is above N5 and is not accepted yet (to decide).

title: Missing verb ending (desu)
context_note: Malay has no copula here; polite Japanese needs です.

title: Mixed: word order and particle deletion
intended_meaning_en: I buy a book at the shop.
accepted_answers_ja: 私は店で本を買います。
私は本を店で買います。
context_note: The verb is not at the end and を is missing.
